trial_court: Family Courts, Tis Hazari Courts (West), Delhi 2, MAT.APP.(F.C.) 49/2024
case_name: Smt Reeta Jha vs Sh Mukund Kumar Jha
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The parties got married in an arranged marriage. The respondent had no uterus and could not conceive. The petitioner wanted to have children but the respondent avoided discussing it. The trial court declared the marriage as null and void under Section 12(1)(c) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: Concealment of a material fact or circumstance concerning the respondent can be a ground for annulment of marriage.
legal_principles.held: The concealment, of the fact of not having a uterus by the petitioner, amounted to concealment of a material fact or circumstance concerning the respondent.
cited_cases: Vandana J Kasliwal V. jitendra N. Kasliwal (2006)
Smt Reeta Jha vs Sh Mukund Kumar Jha (2025)

legal_principles.principle: A material fact or circumstance concerning the respondent must be something which goes to the root of the matter, which would weigh with any prudent person to change his mind.
legal_principles.held: It most not be easily detectable. The Court would be very circumspect, cautious and pragmatic in identifying such fact or circumstance.
cited_cases: Vandana J Kasliwal V. jitendra N. Kasliwal (2006)
Smt Reeta Jha vs Sh Mukund Kumar Jha (2025)

outcome.result: Appeal preferred against the Judgment and Decree dated 05.11.2024
outcome.final_order: The appeal was allowed and the marriage was declared null and void under Section 12(1)(c) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
